name: Target heart rate
seoTitle: Target heart rate — Free Online Calculator
seoDesc: Target heart rate: work out age from the resting heart rate and the target heart rate. A free sports calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: Give the Target heart rate calculator the resting heart rate and the target heart rate and it returns age. Think of it as a shortcut for a training session, a performance comparison or a competition result. Editing anything puts the results away until the next press of Calculate — change one value at a time and the updated answer tells you what that value was worth.

sections.title: How does the Target heart rate calculator work?
sections.html:
The Target heart rate calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports age in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the intensity of your exercise); then you type in the resting heart rate and the target heart rate.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
• A number, expressed in bpm.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 6 options, such as moderate (50-60%), fat burning (60-70%) and aerobic (70-80%). The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • A number, expressed in bpm.

One field on this form is a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the Target heart rate calculator
sections.html:
One relationship drives the whole page:

Age=(-100 × target heart rate + intensity percentage × (220 − resting heart rate) + 100 × resting heart rate) ÷ intensity percentage

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Suppose Resting heart rate = 10, Intensity of your exercise set to Moderate (50-60%), Intensity percentage = 10 and Target heart rate = 10. Working through the relationship above gives Age = 210.

The point of the example is the scale, not the particular digits: swap in your own figures and the same relationship produces your answer.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Age = 210 should be roughly the size you expected from Resting heart rate = 10 and Intensity of your exercise set to Moderate (50-60%).

sections.html:

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Target heart rate calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Comparing two athletes or two attempts fairly
  • Planning a session around a target you already know
  • Tracking progress across a training block
  • Any time the same 2 figures keep coming back — the resting heart rate and the target heart rate — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

sections.title: What are the limits worth knowing?
sections.html:
Every tool draws a boundary somewhere. For the Target heart rate calculator, these are the ones that matter:

  • The 1 drop-down on this page offers a fixed list of cases. A value that is not on the list cannot be entered, and the nearest option is not always a good substitute.
  • The calculator reports what the relationship implies; it does not judge whether the inputs themselves are sensible, so a figure that is out by a factor of ten will produce an answer that is out by the same factor.

faq.q: What does the Target heart rate calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns age, derived from the resting heart rate and the target heart rate. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Target heart rate calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the resting heart rate and the target heart rate, which is 3 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There is one choice to make (1 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Age = 210. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Target heart rate calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
